description.summary: window decorations drawn by a shell

protocol.description: Lets one client, usually a shell, draw the decorations of Leme's windows with its own surfaces. Leme offers every managed window as a leme_decoration_window_v1 with its state, and places the client's decoration surfaces around it. Leme's built-in titlebar stays hidden on a window while one of the client's decorations is visible there.

interface.name: leme_decoration_manager_v1
interface.description: Only one manager is active at a time. A manager bound while another is active receives unavailable and stays inert. When the active manager is destroyed, its windows and decorations go inert and the next manager bound becomes active.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops decorating. Window and decoration objects created through this manager go inert, and Leme's built-in titlebars come back.

event.name: unavailable
event.description: Another manager is active. This manager stays inert and receives no window events.

event.name: window
event.description: Sent when a managed window maps or a window group forms, and for each of them when the manager becomes active. A group carries the group state, the title and app_id of its focused member and the size of its content area; its decorations frame the whole group, and its requests act on the group. The window's id, title, app_id, state and size events follow, closed by done.

interface.name: leme_decoration_window_v1
interface.description: State events come in batches closed by done. After closed, Leme ignores requests on this object and its decorations, and the client should destroy them.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface already has a role or a buffer

entry.name: client_decorated
entry.summary: the client draws its own titlebar

entry.name: grouped
entry.summary: a member of a window group, decorations stay hidden

entry.name: group
entry.summary: a window group; its members report grouped

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the object. Its decorations go inert.

request.name: get_decoration

description.summary: give a surface the decoration role

request.description: Makes the surface a decoration of this window. The surface must have no role and no buffer attached, or the role error is raised.

request.name: move
request.description: Starts moving the window with the pointer, as xdg_toplevel.move does. The serial must be the seat's latest button press.

request.name: resize
request.description: Starts resizing the window with the pointer, as xdg_toplevel.resize does. Edges take the xdg_toplevel.resize_edge values.

request.name: show_window_menu
request.description: Opens Leme's window menu at a point relative to the content's top left corner.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description: Tells Leme that the decorations for the batch ending in done(serial) are committed, or that the client draws none for this window. Leme holds a new window's open animation for a short time until the active client acknowledges the window's first batch.

event.name: id
event.description: The id Leme's control socket uses for this window. It stays the same while Leme runs, across closed and a later window event.

event.name: size
event.description: The size Leme configured for the window content, in logical pixels, without borders or decorations.

event.name: done
event.description: Ends a batch of state events. The client answers with ack_configure after committing its decorations for the new state.

event.name: closed
event.description: The window unmapped or stopped being managed. A new window event offers it again if it comes back.

interface.name: leme_decoration_v1
interface.description: Offset, margins, states and border are double-buffered and apply on the surface's next commit. A decoration is visible when the window's state is in its states mask and the window is not grouped. The window's state is the first of fullscreen, maximized, tiled, desktop and floating that holds. Below decorations stack under the window borders, above decorations over the content and Leme's titlebar.

entry.name: replaced
entry.summary: the decoration draws the border instead

request.name: destroy
request.description: Removes the decoration and its margins from the window.

request.name: set_offset
request.description: Places the surface relative to the window content's top left corner. The initial offset is 0, 0.

request.name: set_margins
request.description: Reserves space between the window content and its borders while the decoration is visible. Margins of visible decorations add up per edge. The initial margins are 0.

request.name: set_states
request.description: The window states in which the decoration is visible. The initial mask is floating, tiled, maximized and desktop.

request.name: set_border
request.description: With replaced, Leme draws no border on the window while the decoration is visible, and the decoration's margins are the whole frame. The initial value is kept.
